name: Resume Builder
tagline: A resume aimed at one specific job: impact-first bullets, a one-page PDF, and a tailored version for each application.
who: Anyone who has to hand someone a resume: a student applying to a club or a first internship, a new grad, a mid-career operator changing lanes, a veteran with twenty years to fit on two pages. Also the parent, manager, or friend who keeps getting asked to look at one.
how:
Your agent asks what you are applying to and where you are in your career. Then:

- It reads whatever you drop in, including old resumes, a LinkedIn export, reviews and project notes, into a master record of everything true about you, with each fact tagged by where it came from.
- A short impact interview turns duties into results with numbers, in Google's "accomplished X, as measured by Y, by doing Z" shape.
- A target brief pulls the posting's own vocabulary and the two or three reasons you fit the role.
- The bundled renderer produces a print-quality PDF in one of six looks, matched to the field and to how you want to come across. Every look is single column with selectable text, which is what both screeners and fast human readers handle best.
- A live preview tab shows the printed pages as they change while you work together, with a menu to switch the look and a color picker for the accent.

At the end you download the PDF and a Word copy, and you keep the master record, so the next application is a tailored version in minutes. Every number traces to something you said or gave it.
